anchor.statement: Proposition 5.5. There are smooth axisymmetric fields (u B , p B ) for q > 0 and two physical tangential stress components T phys , supported where X a ≤ X(r, z, t) ≤ X b , such that div u B = 0 and R (u B , p B ) = −( ∂ r + 2/r)T phys, θ e θ − ( ∂ r + 1/r)T phys,z e z + E B . (5.41) For every fixed 0 < X max < ∞ , uniformly on the profile rectangle [0, X max ] × [−1, 1] in (X, η ), for every Cartesian space-time derivative ∂ α and every M > 0, | ∂ αE B | ≤ C α ,M q M as q ↓ 0. The constants may depend on X max . The formal expansion of (u B , p B , T phys ) has the finite truncations U [N] from Proposition 5.3, with the physical Stokes streamfunctions S n from (5.27) summed before differentiation. Fix radial endpoints 0 < X lo < X a < X b < X hi < ∞ . The rectangle [X lo , X hi ] × [−1, 1] is the fixed radial enlargement of the closed active annulus [X a , X b ] × [−1, 1] from Theorem 4.6(ii), with η ranging over its full closed parameter interval. Uniformly on this enlarged rectangle, for every fixed composition D I of q ∂q , ∂X , ∂ η , as q ↓ 0, D I (q A u θ ,B − E 0 ) = O I (q 2h ), D I (q A u z,B − U 0 ) = O I (q 2h ), D I (q 1/2 u r,B − V 0 / √ 2X) = O I (q 2h ), D I (q A u r,B ) = O I (q h ). (5.42) The constants in these estimates may depend on the fixed radial endpoints. With ˆ︁ T = q A+1/2 T phys , the weighted comparison uses ζ , δ from Theorem 4.6(iv) and holds on X a < X < X b , −1 ≤ η ≤ 1: | D I ( ˆ︁ T − T 0 )| ≤ C I q 2h ζδ −N I ≤ C I q h ζδ −N I (0 < q ≤ 1). (5.43) Every fixed physical space-time derivative of u B , p B , T phys , E B extends continuously to η = ±1 on compact sets with q > 0. The positive-order corrections u B − u (0) and p B − p (0) vanish for X ≥ X + , with X + from Lemma 5.2; in particular the leading profile’s exact exterior (4.29) is preserved. On the reserved interval X ∈ I mean ⊂ (X a , X v ) from Theorem 4.6(vi), for every −1 ≤ η ≤ 1, the base velocity agrees exactly with the leading profile: u B = u (0) , u z,B = 0, q A u θ ,B = E 0 = c patch (1 + η 2 ) −1 X −1/2− λ. (5.44) Here u (0) denotes the velocity determined by the leading profile in (4.3).

correspondence.note: (5.43) is stated only in its weaker form, with C q^h ζ δ^{−N} on the right; of (5.42) only the swirl and axial estimates are stated, and (5.44) for those two components. Not stated in these declarations: the two radial-velocity estimates in (5.42), continuous extension of derivatives to η = ±1, and vanishing of the positive-order corrections for X ≥ X+.

finite PDE identity, support estimate, or residual estimate among the inputs.
The same profile, coefficient sequence, and scale sequence occur throughout.
